theme: The man born blind; the Good Shepherd
readingInstruction: Read John 9:1-10:21. Jesus heals a man born blind, the Pharisees interrogate him, and Jesus then speaks of himself as the door and the good shepherd. Follow the blind man’s growth from not knowing, to knowing, to worship.
settingTheScene: Still in Jerusalem, Jesus passes a man who has been blind from birth. The disciples ask whose sin caused it, a common assumption. Jesus gives another answer. What follows is a masterpiece of storytelling: the healing, a series of interrogations, and the man’s confession. It leads into Jesus’ words about the sheep and the shepherd, which echo Ezekiel 34, where God promises to shepherd his scattered flock.
observation: “It was not that this man sinned, or his parents, but that the works of God might be displayed in him” (9:3).
“One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see” (9:25).
“For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind” (9:39).
“I am the door. If anyone enters by me, he will be saved and will go in and out and find pasture” (10:9).
“I came that they may have life and have it abundantly” (10:10).
“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep” (10:11).
“So there will be one flock, one shepherd” (10:16).
“No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord” (10:18).
interpretation:
Jesus rejects the idea that this man’s blindness was the direct result of someone’s sin. It was so that the works of God might be displayed in him. He spits on the ground, makes mud, anoints the man’s eyes, and tells him to wash in the pool of Siloam. The man goes, washes, and returns seeing.

The neighbors can hardly believe it, and the Pharisees investigate. It was the Sabbath again. The man’s answers grow bolder at each stage. First: “The man called Jesus made mud.” Then: “He is a prophet.” When the leaders press him, he says, “One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see.” He cannot explain everything, but he knows what happened. They mock him, and he says, with a touch of irony, “Do you also want to become his disciples?” They throw him out. Jesus finds him and asks, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?” “Lord, I believe,” he says, and worships. The blind man sees, and those who claim to see remain blind.

Jesus then turns to the image of the sheep. The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. Jesus has come that his sheep may have life and have it abundantly. He is the door: whoever enters through him will be saved. He is also the good shepherd, who knows his sheep by name, and whom the sheep know. The hired hand flees when the wolf comes, but the shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

Notice the contrast. The false shepherds, the religious leaders who cast out the blind man, care for themselves. Jesus, the true shepherd, seeks the outcast. He says he has other sheep who are not of this fold, a reference to the Gentiles, and “there will be one flock, one shepherd.” And his death is no accident: “No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have authority to lay it down, and authority to take it up again.”

The Father’s command and the Son’s authority are in harmony. The shepherd dies willingly, and rises. The people divide again over his words. This is the third and fourth of the “I AM” sayings, the door and the good shepherd.
connection: Psalm 23 and Ezekiel 34 are the great shepherd passages. Isaiah 35:5 and 42:7 promise sight for the blind. Isaiah 42:16 says God will lead the blind in a way they do not know. Jeremiah 23:1-4 condemns false shepherds. Zechariah 11 pictures the rejected shepherd. 1 Peter 2:25 says we have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of our souls. Hebrews 13:20 calls Jesus the great shepherd of the sheep. Revelation 7:17 says the Lamb will be their shepherd.
application:
Tell someone your own “I was blind, but now I see” in a sentence or two.

Listen for the shepherd’s voice in his word today. What is he saying to you?

Pray for someone who has been cast out or hurt by the church. Ask Jesus to find them.
prayerPrompts: Tell Jesus, “I was blind, and now I see,” and name something he has shown you.
Ask him to help you hear the Shepherd’s voice.
